name: OR-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic partisan lean in a favorable environment
Incumbent Val Hoyle's two-to-one fundraising advantage over Monique DeSpain
Prediction markets price Hoyle at roughly 96% to win
No public general-election polling to refine the estimate
model.rationale: OR-04 leans Democratic by six points and the national environment adds to that, while Hoyle has out-raised DeSpain substantially and holds more cash on hand. Markets price her near certain, so the forecast stays safely Democratic with a modest trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or surge of outside spending against Hoyle could tighten the race toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Val Hoyle seeks reelection in a southwestern Oregon district that leans Democratic by about six points. She has raised roughly $1.2 million to Monique DeSpain's $677,000 and holds a cash advantage, with outside groups spending modestly on both sides. Prediction markets give Hoyle about a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

The main uncertainty is the lack of public general-election polling, so the margin rests on fundamentals. A Democratic-leaning seat, an incumbent's financial edge, and favorable market pricing all point the same direction, making Hoyle the clear favorite despite some room for error in the exact margin.
